title: Canary: add A/B runner (baseline vs mixed-workload scheduler) + publish summary to dashboards
author: Sana Farid
body:
Context
We need a reliable, repeatable A/B signal for the mixed-workload scheduler prototype (short/long prompt-aware scheduling) before we can do the limited production slice. Today perf-canary runs a single configuration and publishes raw run artifacts, but we’re missing:
- A/B comparisons in the same job window (baseline vs scheduler flag on)
- A standardized summary artifact (so dashboards can read it)
- Guardrails around warmup, ordering effects, and noisy runs

This PR extends perf-canary to run paired A/B jobs and publish a small metrics + JSON summary to Grafana dashboards used by runtime + SRE.

What’s in this PR
- New “ab_compare” mode in the canary workflow that executes the same benchmark suite twice:
  - A (baseline): mixed-workload scheduler flag OFF
  - B (candidate): mixed-workload scheduler flag ON (and optional classifier config override)
- Controls to reduce measurement bias:
  - Same build SHA and hardware pool
  - Fixed benchmark seed per scenario (propagated into the runner)
  - Warmup phase before each arm
  - Randomized arm order per job (default on) with the order recorded in artifacts
- A/B summary generation:
  - Computes deltas for key metrics: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency, queue wait p95, time-to-first-token (TTFT) p95, throughput (tok/s), and GPU util
  - Emits a single JSON summary file and a single compact text table
- Publishing:
  - Pushes summary metrics as Prometheus gauges with labels (scenario, model, sku, arm, run_id)
  - Uploads JSON/text artifacts to the job run
  - Posts a short comment to the perf-canary Slack hook (existing integration) with pass/fail and links
- Default thresholds (non-blocking for now):
  - p95 latency improvement expected >= 5% on mixed workloads
  - throughput regression allowed up to 3% (warn above, do not fail yet)
  - starvation signal: long-queue wait p99 must not exceed baseline by > 10% (warn)

Why this shape
We want to keep “policy correctness” checks (fairness/starvation simulation, etc.) in runtime CI, and use perf-canary for stable signal on realistic infra + runtime builds. This PR stays focused on orchestration + publishing, and leaves policy definition to runtime.

Operational notes
- The A/B canary job is gated behind a workflow input and will not replace the existing single-arm canary until we’ve validated stability.
- Metrics are namespaced under perf_canary_ab_* to avoid colliding with existing panels.

Follow-ups
- After 1–2 weeks of A/B data, we should flip the canary default to A/B for mixed-workload scenarios and make the throughput regression threshold blocking (requires Jonas + SRE sign-off).

Test plan
- Ran locally with mocked runner output to validate JSON + Prometheus emission.
- Triggered staging canary runs on 2 SKUs (A10 + H100) with a small scenario set; verified:
  - both arms ran
  - artifacts uploaded
  - dashboard panels populated

Example summary excerpt
scenario=mixed_prompt_len_pareto_80_20 model=llama-3-70b sku=h100
p95_latency_ms: A=412.3 B=351.8 (-14.7%)
throughput_tok_s: A=11854 B=11690 (-1.4%)
long_queue_wait_p99_ms: A=932 B=948 (+1.7%)
commits: workflow: add ab_compare inputs + arm randomization
runner: implement paired execution and warmup accounting
summary: compute deltas + emit compact table + json artifact
publishing: export A/B metrics to Prometheus + add labels
docs: update runbook and dashboard pointers
review_conversation:
Jonas Weber (review): Can we guarantee we don’t compare runs from different SHAs if the job restarts? Also, I’d like the summary to record the arm order and warmup duration explicitly.
Sana Farid (author): Good call. Added build_sha to the run manifest and summary. Also recording arm_order, warmup_seconds, and scenario_seed in the JSON.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Please make sure the scheduler flag is surfaced as a single knob (env var is fine) and that we can pass classifier overrides (thresholds/EWMA) as a blob without editing the workflow each time.
Sana Farid (author): Added workflow inputs: scheduler_flag (bool) and scheduler_config_json (string). The runner passes it through to the runtime launcher.

Aisha Bello (review): Metric naming: can we avoid high-cardinality labels? run_id is OK but don’t add commit message, etc. Also add a ‘result=pass|warn|fail’ label so dashboards can filter.
Sana Farid (author): Kept labels to scenario/model/sku/arm/run_id/build_sha. Added result label at the summary level; per-metric we expose result via a separate gauge perf_canary_ab_result{...}.

Rafael Mendes (review): From an on-call POV, I need a single link and a single table in Slack. Also, warn loudly if only one arm ran.
Sana Farid (author): Slack message now includes a compact table and links to artifacts + Grafana. Added explicit ‘incomplete_ab=true’ in the summary and Slack text if either arm fails.

Felix Schneider (review): Please confirm this is compatible with the existing dashboard templates. We’ll need the metric names stable.
Sana Farid (author): Added docs/runbooks/ab-canary.md with the exact metric list; pinned names under perf_canary_ab_* and added a small compatibility section.

Jonas Weber (approval): Looks good. Non-blocking thresholds are the right call for now. Let’s collect data before turning this into a gate.
Aisha Bello (approval): Approved with the label/cardinality constraints as implemented.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved.
